status_summary: No action reviving the comprehensive account reporting proposal was found. Public Law 119-21, approved 2025-07-04, restored in section 70432 the earlier de minimis rule for third party network transaction reporting on Form 1099-K (reporting only above $20,000 and 200 transactions, effective as if included in the 2021 American Rescue Plan Act provision that had lowered it), and in section 70433 raised the payee information reporting threshold in 26 U.S.C. 6041(a) from $600 to $2,000 for payments made after 2025-12-31, with cost-of-living indexing for calendar years after 2026, as shown in the U.S. Code amendment notes. The IRS stated on 2025-10-23 that the law retroactively reinstated the earlier Form 1099-K threshold. These reduce specific reporting burdens; no broader review of the information reporting regime was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was approved; its table of contents lists Section 70432 on third party network transaction reporting and Section 70433 raising the payee information reporting threshold.

Public Law 119-21 section 70432 amended 26 U.S.C. 6050W(e) so that third party settlement organizations report third party network transactions only above $20,000 and 200 transactions, effective as if included in section 9674 of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, which had lowered the threshold to $600.

title: Oppose comprehensive $600 bank account reporting and cut information reporting burdens
uncertainties: The Form 1099-K threshold that the law restored was set by a 2021 statute and is distinct from the account reporting proposal the Mandate opposes; the Mandate mentions Form 1099-K only as part of that proposal, so the threshold changes are treated as partial progress on the burden-reduction item. The govinfo.gov HTML of Public Law 119-21 is cut off in the first title, so sections 70432 and 70433 are confirmed from the U.S. Code reproductions of 26 U.S.C. 6050W and 6041 hosted by law.cornell.edu (amendment notes read on 2026-10-22). The form-level effect on Forms 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC rests on a trade publication and an external retrieval and was not verified on irs.gov or in the Code pages. An external retrieval also reports conforming changes to 26 U.S.C. 6041A and to backup withholding, with a backup withholding start for calendar years beginning after 2024-12-31; these were not seen on the pages opened. Whether any later budget request revived the account reporting proposal was not searched.
